headline: Nobel-winning economist Michael Spence pushed back on fears that AI will wipe out 40% of jobs, saying its impact will arrive gradually.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: only a short video description was available, so what Spence actually said is unverified.
importance_line: Workers and policymakers weighing job-loss forecasts are affected, but we have only the publisher's one-paragraph description of an interview, not what he said.
summary: The Economic Times says in its description of a short video that Nobel laureate economist Michael Spence pushes back on fears that AI could wipe out 40% of jobs, arguing its impact will unfold gradually as businesses adapt.
notes: Video page; only the publisher's description was readable. No transcript.
